title: T2 · Event-probability shocks and the assets they move
decision: T2 works as a risk tool: Polymarket shocks move the assets they relate to (event exposure monitor). Shocks also predict the next hour's direction: add alerts. Skilled wallets move first: add a wallet early-warning layer.

experiments.title: Data
experiments.question: Are there enough contested event markets overlapping with asset trading hours?
experiments.headline: 689 event markets aligned with hourly prices of 26 assets; 7,156 shock hours.
notes: Pass rule: ≥ 100 markets with aligned mapped assets.

experiments.title: Same-hour sensitivity
experiments.question: When an event's probability jumps, do the assets linked to that event move more than unrelated assets?
experiments.headline: In shock hours, related assets move +0.25× (of normal-hour size) more than unrelated assets (95% CI +0.15 to +0.34, 366 markets). Without crypto-price markets: +0.22× (CI +0.11 to +0.34).
notes: Direction-free test (a market's YES can be good or bad news for an asset).
Pass rule: mapped-minus-placebo ratio > 0 with the 95% CI above 0 (bootstrap over markets); fewer than 30 markets = inconclusive.

experiments.title: Next-hour lead
experiments.question: Does a probability shock tell us where the related asset goes in the following hour?
experiments.headline: Next-hour direction after shocks: hit rate 53.1% (95% CI 50.6% to 55.5%, 343 markets). Next-hour size effect vs unrelated assets: -0.01× (CI -0.08 to +0.06).
notes: Direction uses the sign of each market-asset co-movement estimated on earlier hours only.
Pass rule (direction): hit rate above 50% with the 95% CI above 50%; < 30 markets = inconclusive. The size effect is reported as secondary (useful for a volatility warning).

experiments.title: Skilled wallets lead the probability
experiments.question: Does net buying by skilled wallets predict the next hour's probability move?
experiments.headline: After an hour of net skilled-wallet buying (≥ $500), the probability moves +0.70 points their way next hour (95% CI +0.03 to +1.31, 170 markets); everyone else: +0.53.
notes: Skill is point-in-time (topic F's timeline: markets closed before each trade).
Pass rule: skilled-flow signed next-hour move > 0 with the 95% CI above 0; < 30 markets = inconclusive.

experiments.title: Stable exposures
experiments.question: If an asset rose with an event's probability early on, does it still do so later?
experiments.headline: Exposure keeps its sign in 44% of related market-asset pairs (95% CI 34% to 54%, 42 markets).
notes: Exposure = slope of hourly asset return on hourly change in the event's log-odds.
Pass rule: sign agreement above 50% with the 95% CI above 50%.
